note: Rejudged RFC 7296 Section 2.24's requirement to implement tunnel encapsulation and decapsulation processing to prevent discarding ECN congestion indications. The existing installer tests read actual directional Child SA descriptions and refuse vacuous/uninitialized subjects; the XFRM tests read production xfrmStateFromParams output and distinguish tunnel and transport, with no ECN-disabling field set. The VPP capture tests assert both ENCAP_COPY_ECN and DECAP_COPY_ECN in the actual SAD message and verify refused transport mode sends no message. The changed TestRFC7296BareESPOnTemplatedSAKeepsTheOuterCE adds a real lower-layer observation under the production SPD for both alternate bare-ESP receive paths: a whole datagram must increment the tc rewrite count exactly once, a deliberately oversized fragmented datagram must increment reassembly and leave tc rewrite count unchanged, and both must deliver inner TOS exactly 0x03 from ECN-capable 0x02 under outer CE. The current receiver preserves the received TOS through writeESPForm, and the fast rewrite keeps the received TOS octet. The test therefore distinguishes paths and directly detects losing CE on either; the new counter/selector machinery does not invalidate the ECN assertions. No claim about mixed protection-context separation is inferred from this ECN test.
